articles.summary: With the 78th Emmy Awards well underway, it’s officially TV’s biggest night — which means the stars are hitting the red carpet in their Monday best. Heading into the evening, HBO Max’s medical drama “The Pitt” leads with 25 nominations, followed closely by “Hacks,” also from the streamer, with 24.
body: Following closely behind is Apple TV’s horror comedy hit “Window’s Bay” with 19 nominations, and Apple TV’s “Pluribus” with 18. NBC’s “Saturday Night Live” leads with 11 nominations on the broadcast network side.

Sterling K. Brown (“Paradise”), Gary Oldman (“Slow Horses”), Mark Ruffalo (“Task”), Rufus Sewell (“The Diplomat”) and Noah Wyle (“The Pitt”) are all nominated for the Emmy Award for best actor in a drama series. In the lead actress in a drama series category, the nominees include Carrie Coon (“The Gilded Age”), Chase Infiniti (“The Testaments”), Keri Russell (“The Diplomat”), Rhea Seehorn (“Pluribus”) and Zendaya (“Euphoria”).

articles.title: Jeremy Thomas obituary
articles.summary: Film producer who enjoyed his greatest success with the 1987 epic The Last Emperor for which he won an Oscar. Asked whether he had ever cautioned restraint from a director, the film producer Jeremy Thomas replied: “My nature would be to go further and see what we can get away with.” Thomas, who has…
body: Thomas, who has died aged 77, was an expert in getting away with it. A taste for irreverence ran in his family: he was the son of Ralph Thomas, director of the Doctor … comedies that began in 1954 with Doctor in the House, and the nephew of Gerald Thomas, who made all 31 Carry On titles. Jeremy’s own films, however, were risky rather than risque.

Bad Timing (1980), the first of three collaborations with the director Nicolas Roeg, explored a destructive love affair blighted by jealousy, attempted suicide and rape. Rank, the studio behind it, withheld from the start of the print its familiar company ident showing a man striking a gong. According to Thomas, the studio also denounced the picture as “a sick film made by sick people for sick people”.

He teamed up on several occasions with David Cronenberg, first for an adaptation of William S Burroughs’s Naked Lunch (1991), featuring a sentient, fleshy typewriter that talks through its anus, and most infamously for a film of Crash (1996), JG Ballard’s novel about a group of outsiders who get their sexual kicks from car accidents.
points: Film producer who enjoyed his greatest success with the 1987 epic The Last Emperor for which he won an Oscar.

articles.title: Henry Winkler Refused to Let ABC Change ‘Happy Days’ Title to ‘Fonzie’s Happy Days’ Because ‘It Would Be a Slap in the Face’ to Co-Stars
articles.summary: Henry Winkler opened up on the latest episode of “In Depth With Graham Bensinger” about refusing to let ABC executives change the name of “Happy Days” to “Fonzie’s Happy Days” due to the explosive popularity of his character.
body: Winkler was also concerned about keeping tensions among the ensemble cast at bay. According to the actor, Ron Howard was already annoyed with Fonz becoming the show’s breakout character and felt he was being “overshadowed” by him. Howard played the show’s original lead character Richie Cunningham, leaving “Happy Days” after seven seasons.

“[Ron] said, ‘Look, it hurt my feelings. You’re not doing anything to hurt my feelings. You’re really good and you’re good for the show. It’s helping the show. So I put all of that together and that’s the way it is.’ And we never talked about it again,” Winkler said of Howard’s annoyances.

Regardless, Winkler wanted to keep the peace among the cast and turned down the title change because “we can’t do [the show] if we are resentful or angry of each other.” The actor also turned down Goldenson’s offer to spin off Fonz into his own series because “I have no idea if I’d have a chemistry with new people.” Winkler told the ABC boss: “I don’t think I can do my own show. I think I’m very happy right where I am with this extraordinary family.”

articles.title: In an age of superhero fatigue, Marvel’s best shot is to think small – and outside the box
articles.summary: Sebastian Stan says he pitched Marvel a mid-budget thriller starring his Winter Soldier character. Perhaps the studio should give it – and other modestly scaled vehicles – the green light. Blink a little and you might think we are back in 2019.
body: And yet it doesn’t really feel like it, largely because it is something of a turnaround for Marvel, after a pretty disappointing 2025 in which all three of the studio’s releases underperformed. Captain America: Brave New World took $415m worldwide, Thunderbolts* managed $382m and even the well-reviewed The Fantastic Four: First Steps stalled at $521m, against a reported $200m budget. These are hardly Madame Web numbers but they do suggest there is still a problem about what to do with all those superheroes who cannot sustain a $300m multiversal extravaganza.

Enter Sebastian Stan, AKA Marvel’s Winter Soldier, who this week suggested the solution might be to place them in cheaper genre films instead. Speaking to New York Magazine, the actor revealed that he had pitched Marvel boss Kevin Feige a new, “Sicario-esque”” approach for Bucky Barnes’ next adventure. “We keep a real small budget,” he said. “It’s about a guy who thinks he recog­nises someone from his past that had something to do with when, you know, he was brain­washed, and he gets obsessed with this per­son. He goes on a whole jour­ney to try to fig­ure out who this per­son is. It’s a thriller.”

articles.title: Barrio Triste review – raw and dynamic portrait of anarchic slum life in 1980s Medellín
articles.summary: Bad Bunny collaborator Stillz’s debut feature shot using Betacam focuses on vibes over plot. Best known as the creative mind behind the music videos of Puerto Rican rapper and singer Bad Bunny, Stillz has risen to the top of the industry as an in-demand director and photographer.
body: There are moments of crisis here and there – the restless band of youths attempt a robbery and even kill a hostage – yet the primary focus seems to be on vibes rather than plot. The ever-roving camera not only channels the agitated psyche of the main characters but also drums up the chaotic pace of Medellín’s underbelly. One particularly memorable sequence moves from the peculiar sight of a punk duo practising on a rooftop to the garbage-strewn streets, during which seemingly benign interactions can quickly escalate into heated altercations. Echoing the handheld cinematography, life in the slums is unmoored and precarious, as if the ground might give way at any second.
points: Bad Bunny collaborator Stillz’s debut feature shot using Betacam focuses on vibes over plot.

articles.title: Legendary costume designer Bob Mackie dies aged 87
articles.summary: The "Sultan of Sequins" created iconic and dazzling costumes for stars including Cher, Tina Turner and Elton John.
body: Bob Mackie, who designed dazzling costumes for stars including Cher, Tina Turner, Dolly Parton and Elton John has died, aged 87.
The US fashion designer, known as the "Sultan of Sequins" for his sparkling creations, won a Tony Award, nine Emmys and received three Oscar nominations during his career.
"It is with a heavy heart that we share the news that Mr Bob Mackie passed away today," a statement on his Instagram account announced on Monday.

"He lived his 87 years to the fullest, fulfilling his dream of being a Fashion and Costume Designer, which is all he ever wanted to do," it added. "His genius and extraordinary designs will live on forever, continuing to bring beauty into this world."

articles.title: Macklemore dropped from Ed Sheeran tour after 'Free Palestine' speech
articles.summary: The US rapper was condemned by Jewish groups after making comments criticising Israel.
body: Rapper Macklemore has been dropped from Ed Sheeran's US tour after making pro-Palestinian comments on stage earlier this month.

The artist - whose real name is Benjamin Haggerty - had been the opening act for Sheeran's Loop tour, but was criticised by Jewish groups after saying "Free Palestine" at two concerts and making political speeches.
Macklemore stood by his comments on Monday, confirming that he had been cut from the tour and writing in a statement that the real victims are the Palestinian people in Gaza.
Ed Sheeran has not yet commented, and who will replace Macklemore for the rest of the tour is unknown.

articles.title: The Route to Cappyness review – capybara boosterism is an ode to the internet’s favourite rodent
articles.summary: From a cappy-cafe owner in Japan to an escaped capybara in the UK, this homespun film takes the temperature of an international obsession. One of Midlands-based film-maker Sharon Walia’s previous works was The Keepers of the Pigs, proudly described on her production company’s website as “the first…
body: Walia’s celebration of the species stays on script, rejoicing in the animals’ natural geniality, friendliness to other species in their natural habitat, and their compelling, remunerative charm that seems to have bolstered the fortunes of several animal attractions around the world.

Other interlocutors include a cappy-cafe owner in Japan who’s found a great way to get out of the rat race doing what he loves and makes no claims to expertise on the creatures. By contrast, American cappy shillers love to reel off factoids and anecdotes and all sound like they’ve had media training should a camera crew or schoolbus full of kids pull up to the gates. The British cappy-keepers are endearingly more amateur, yet noticeably a little defensive, especially the owners of the park from where Cinnamon, a young female capybara, escaped and made the news and, once again, social media.

articles.title: The Pitt is up for 25 Emmys - but the show's biggest fans are real-life doctors
articles.summary: Those in the medical profession say the HBO Max show about a US hospital emergency room is the most realistic medical drama yet.
body: It's a familiar sight: a crowded waiting room, trolleys in corridors, stressed doctors and nurses. But this isn't a typical A&E unit in the NHS, it's a Hollywood set with actors recreating the drama of an emergency department for TV series The Pitt.
"We finally feel validated for everything we go through every day," says Dr Tony Cirillo, President of the American College of Emergency Physicians.
On Monday, The Pitt could become this year's most decorated series at the Emmys, America's most coveted TV honours, with 25 nominations.
Doctors and others in the medical profession say, for them, it's the most realistic medical drama yet - which is why they love it.
